evidence.text: Peter Elmsley( 1773 – 1825) was an English classical scholar.

evidence.title: Peter Elmsley
evidence.text: He was educated at Westminster and Christ Church, Oxford, and having inherited a fortune from his uncle, also Peter Elmsley, a well- known bookseller, devoted himself to the study of classical authors and manuscripts.

evidence.title: Peter Elmsley
evidence.text: He took Holy Orders and in 1798 was appointed to the chapelry of Little Horkesley in Essex, which he held until his death.

evidence.title: Peter Elmsley
evidence.text: He was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1814.

evidence.title: Peter Elmsley
evidence.text: He travelled extensively in France and Italy, and spent the winter of 1818 in examining the manuscripts in the Laurentian Library at Florence.

evidence.title: Peter Elmsley
evidence.text: In 1819 he was commissioned, with Sir Humphry Davy, to decipher the papyri found at Herculaneum, but the results proved insignificant.

evidence.title: Peter Elmsley
evidence.text: In 1823 he was appointed principal of St. Alban Hall, Oxford, and Camden Professor of Ancient History.

evidence.title: Peter Elmsley
evidence.text: He died in St Alban Hall, Oxford on 8 March 1825.

evidence.title: Peter Elmsley
evidence.text: Elmsley was a man of most extensive learning and European reputation, and was considered to be the best ecclesiastical scholar in England.
